input.context: Agency asked if job done (booked 30/09/2025) and for PDF invoice. Landlord approved hinge replacement £90 + VAT. No attachment visible in CRM.

input.situation_text: Contractor emailed 'Attached invoice' after job booked for 30/09 but no attachment is visible in the CRM. Landlord approved £90 + VAT hinge replacement.

lessons.situation: A contractor who completed an approved cleaning job emails to say their invoice has been sent to the agency's operator, while the request is on hold waiting for the provider and the system is prompting the operator to check whether a reply is needed or to return the request to auto mode.
lessons.action: When the contractor confirms the invoice has been sent, no reply to them is needed. Move the task to the result/completed state, mark the request as completed for final checks, and forward the invoice to the landlord with a short covering note. Record that landlord confirmation is needed, then close the request once the final checks are done.
lessons.rationale: A contractor's invoice notification is an informational closing message rather than a question, so the right response is to progress closeout and pass the invoice to the landlord instead of replying or leaving the request on hold.

lessons.situation: A contractor attended a scheduled repair visit, but the system showed no work results afterwards and flagged the job for checking; the contractor's invoice note then described the fault found, the fix and a successful test.
lessons.action: When no work results have been logged after a completed visit, check the contractor's invoice note for the findings and outcome, and treat it as the completion record if it confirms the fault, the fix and a passing test. Move the task to Result, mark the request completed and start the final checks. Skip optional document uploads that aren't needed, recording the reason. Then request the landlord's confirmation before closing.
lessons.rationale: The invoice note can serve as proof of completion when no separate report exists, and the landlord should still confirm before the job is closed.

lessons.situation: A landlord who is arranging communal garden works through their own contractor confirms they have received quotes and agree to proceed, but no start date has been given yet.
lessons.action: Acknowledge the landlord's approval and ask them to pass on the contractor's start date as soon as they have it. Put the job on hold with the reason 'Waiting for Landlord' and a note that the start date is pending. Send a short update to the tenants who reported the issue, telling them a contractor has been instructed and that you will confirm the start date once you have it.
lessons.rationale: The landlord is managing the contractor, so the agency cannot schedule the works until the date comes back. Holding the job and keeping the reporting tenants informed avoids chasing too early and stops tenants wondering whether anything is happening.

lessons.situation: A provider has been assigned after landlord approval and has made contact attempts with the tenant (a callback request and a failed call connection), but no booking has been confirmed and nothing in the contact requires an agency reply.
lessons.action: Review the provider's contact attempts to see whether they ask the agency for anything. If they only concern arranging access with the tenant and need no agency response, do not intervene or send new messages. Put the job on hold with the reason 'waiting for provider' and a note that the appointment is still to be booked, then let the provider and tenant sort out the visit and revisit if no booking is confirmed.
lessons.rationale: Provider-tenant call attempts are a normal part of scheduling and need no agency action, so holding with a clear note avoids duplicate chasing while keeping the job visible until the appointment is booked.

lessons.situation: After chasing a landlord for approval of a high-cost specialist waste removal quote, the landlord replies approving the work, and the request has been flagged by the system to check whether a response is needed or to return it to auto mode.
lessons.action: Treat the landlord's approval as the go-ahead: do not return the request to auto mode yet. Instruct the contractor to arrange the removal and keep the job on hold with a note that it is being arranged. Then contact the tenant straight away with the contractor's available dates to arrange access, asking for prompt confirmation. If phone calls go unanswered, follow up in writing, and switch the hold reason to waiting for the tenant once the access request has been sent.
lessons.rationale: Landlord approval removes the blocker, but the job still needs contractor booking and tenant access confirmed, so it needs active human-style coordination rather than being handed back to automation.
